---
title: "Sources and licences"
---

Transcription begins with someone else's artifact, which gives source keeping a
musical as well as a legal purpose. The exact edition or recording determines
what you can inspect, share, and return to when two details disagree. This
ledger records that provenance. Lesson 42 walks through an entry before any
external file reaches the repository.

Public-domain status differs by country. A modern typeset edition of an old work
can also carry rights of its own even when the composition is free to use. The
composer's death date begins the inquiry; the exact edition and recording finish
it.

## First-draft inventory

The first draft distributes no third-party score, MIDI file, or recording. Its
manuscript, Sonic Pi examples, and exercise melodies were generated by GPT 5.6
Sol at High Reasoning. They are undergoing revision and independent testing; no
human-authored edition is claimed.

| Material | Draft creator | Source | Used in |

| Lesson prose and original exercise melodies | GPT 5.6 Sol at High Reasoning | This repository | Throughout |
| Sonic Pi code examples | GPT 5.6 Sol at High Reasoning | This repository | Throughout |
| Musical Equalizer icon | Gauden Galea | `assets/img/favicon.png` | Site and book identity |

An exercise that asks you to choose a public-domain source does not alter the
rights governing that external artifact. Your copy remains governed by its own
edition, performance, and recording terms.

## Where to look

| Source | What it holds | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| [IMSLP](https://imslp.org/) | Scanned scores and parts from many periods | Item status, edition rights, and permitted use vary by jurisdiction |
| [Mutopia](https://www.mutopiaproject.org/) | Typeset scores offered with item-level terms | Verify the displayed terms and the source edition |
| [MuseScore](https://musescore.com/) | Community scores and arrangements | Access and rights vary per upload; an available score is not automatic permission to redistribute |

These links help you discover material; they do not establish permission for a
particular item. Save the item page, file, and licence statement together.
Availability and national public-domain rules can change independently.
IMSLP's own [public-domain guidance](https://imslp.org/wiki/Public_domain)
states that status varies between countries and does not guarantee that its
general information is legally accurate for a particular use.

## Record one item

Use one row per exact artifact. “Bach minuet” is insufficient because the
composition, edition, typesetting, performance, and recording can each have a
different rightsholder.

| Field | Record |
|---|---|
| Piece | Work title and catalogue number where one exists |
| Composer | Name plus death year used for the public-domain check |
| Source | Stable page address, archive identifier, or repository path |
| Edition | Editor, publisher, date, and scan or typeset identifier |
| Performance | Performer and recording date if audio is used |
| Licence | Exact licence or public-domain mark shown by the source |
| Retrieved | Date the artifact and its rights statement were saved |
| Used in | Lesson and measure or time range |

Store a local note beside the artifact when a judgement is involved. A useful
note states the rule applied and the evidence checked. It should not claim that
the same rule holds in every country.

## Candidate-source worksheet

The transcription chapters ask you to select short material rather than require

published edition.

| Piece | Composer | Source | Edition or recording | Licence evidence | Intended lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader-selected four-bar melody | To be recorded by the reader | Local copy | Exact artifact required | Verify before redistribution | 41-46 |

The placeholder row describes a workflow, not a licensed asset. Replace it only
when the chosen artifact and its evidence are in hand.

## Repository rule

Do not commit an external score or recording because its composition is old.
Commit it when the exact artifact has an entry above, the licence permits this
form of redistribution, and the attribution appears beside every use. A link can
also fail, so keep the retrieval date and enough metadata to find another lawful
copy.

For material that stays on the reader's machine, cite the source in field notes
without copying it into the repository. The code representation you create from
it may still encode a substantial part of the work. Treat publication of that
representation as a separate rights decision.
